questions.question: What is the main difference between singleton and conjunctive visual search?

answers.a: Singleton search involves searching for a specific color, while conjunctive search involves searching for multiple colors.
answers.b: Singleton search is faster and more accurate than conjunctive search.
answers.c: Singleton search involves searching for a target with a single distinct feature, while conjunctive search involves searching for a target defined by a combination of features.
answers.d: Singleton search is more challenging than conjunctive search.

explanations.a: This is incorrect because conjunctive search is not only about multiple colors but also other features like shape.
explanations.b: Although singleton search is generally faster, this option does not fully explain the difference.
explanations.c: Correct! Singleton search focuses on one distinct feature, while conjunctive search requires combining multiple features.
explanations.d: This is incorrect; conjunctive search is more challenging than singleton search.

questions.question: What is a distractor in a visual search task?

answers.a: An object that helps in locating the target.
answers.b: An object that is irrelevant and intended to divert attention from the target.
answers.c: An object that is identical to the target.
answers.d: An object used to speed up response time.

explanations.a: Distractors do not help in locating the target; they are meant to divert attention.
explanations.b: Correct! A distractor is an irrelevant object that makes it harder to find the target.
explanations.c: This is incorrect because distractors are not identical to the target.
explanations.d: Distractors generally slow down response time, not speed it up.

questions.question: How does increasing the set size affect response time in conjunctive search?

answers.a: Response time decreases as set size increases.
answers.b: Response time remains the same regardless of set size.
answers.c: Response time increases because more items need to be analyzed to locate the target.
answers.d: Response time is unaffected in conjunctive search but increases in singleton search.

explanations.a: This is incorrect; increasing the set size generally increases response time in conjunctive search.
explanations.b: This is incorrect because set size directly influences the time needed to locate the target in conjunctive search.
explanations.c: Correct! In conjunctive search, response time increases as the set size grows because more items must be examined.
explanations.d: This is incorrect; conjunctive search is affected by set size, while singleton search is less influenced.
